summary: Riansares fire tower, Clinton County PA: steel tower built 1921, removed in the 1990s; summit cabin still in use; site reached by road.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1990s, per the register and a photo caption. The cabin on the summit remains in use, per the caption.

access.note: A 2023 volunteer notice for a DCNR vista cleanup gives driving directions to the summit and invites volunteers. No gate or permit rule is mentioned.

events.note: Steel tower and its cabin built in 1921 per the photo caption. The register gives 1921; a December 1921 paper calls it the new steel fire tower.
A state forest ranger, Russel E. Berry of Loganton, was in charge (December 1921 paper). This is not confirmed as tower observer work.
Harry E. Lamey was watchman at the tower.
Harry E. Lamey was employed as towerman on the large steel fire tower on Mount Riansares.
Register and photo caption say the tower was removed in the 1990s. The year shown is the start of the decade, not a dated event.
Registered September 16, 2008, nominated by Henry Isenberg.

corrections.why: The 2023 DCNR vista cleanup notice and the photo caption both place the summit in Bald Eagle State Forest. The Eastern lookouts page header says state park, which the other two sources contradict.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1921 paper spells it Rainares and the 1936 paper uses Mount Riansares. The record keeps Riansares, the spelling in the register.

notes_for_editor: Record coordinates (41.0519, -77.3795) come from the Eastern lookouts page; the register lists none. They were not checked against a map. The 1990s removal date is only a decade. The cabin 'in use' claim rests on a single photo caption by an individual photographer. Staffing facts stop in 1938. Access rests on a 2023 volunteer notice; a visit or a DCNR check would confirm it. The 'former fire tower house' in the notice may or may not be the caption's cabin. Record agency corrected from Park to Forest. No photos added.
